text: . Deferiprone: new insight. Ann N Y Acad Sci 2005; 1054: 169–74. Administration in children. UK licensed product informa- tion states that there are limited data on the use of deferiprone in children between 6 and 10 years of age, and no data on use in children below 6. Australian licensed product information states that limited data exist for children between the ages of 2 and 10 but that the effects of deferiprone on growth are unknown. Li- censed doses in children are calculated by weight on the same basis as adults (see Uses and Administration, above). Thalassaemia. Patients with thalassaemia receiving regular blood transfusions commonly develop iron overload requiring use of iron chelators. Deferiprone was developed as an oral alter- native to desferrioxamine, but its role has been controversial. See Thalassaemia under Uses of Desferrioxamine, p.1442, for fur- ther information.
